title: Idle claim holder alarm
current: The fleet watcher reads every live session's full roster row and emits a fleet ALARM idle-holder line for each work-claim holder silent past the idle threshold, parked or not. The line names the session, its items, idle minutes, mode, park reason, native process state (running, exited, resuming, or unknown from a roster that does not serve native_process_exited_at), surface and the item-addressed reach command. A healthy in-flight landing wait, a merged queue landing whose holder has not acted since the landing notice (merge_queue_notified_at), or an item standing at its pinned release wait does not alarm. An idle holder alarm names the nonterminal items whose blocked_by edges name its held items. A parked holder with dependents repeats hourly while they remain; a parked holder without dependents alarms once. An unparked holder repeats hourly while it stays idle. Either emits one fleet CLEAR idle-holder line when activity resumes. Steering answers every alarm in the same turn with an action or a one-line disposition saying why the wait is still sound. Both the report and watcher treat a live newest open long-running call as busy for at most 45 minutes; otherwise idle timing uses last_tool_call_at from real hook tool calls. The sessions.watcher_activity pulse refreshes only session and claim heartbeats. Pulses never count as tool work or suppress undelivered-message alarms; refusal to refresh liveness is named in the wrapper progress capture with recovery. An unsatisfied gating dependency belonging to a held item suppresses its fleet idle-holder alarm through item_awaiting_dependency. Satisfied edges, coordination_only edges and fact:deployed:<env> edges do not suppress it; deployment facts have no satisfaction wake. A silent holder that holds a consumed QA_HOST lease alarms whether parked, awaiting or not, and the line carries qa_hosts=<machines>; the steering report row names the held host. It fires before control-plane upkeep returns the host to the line after qa_host_idle_hold_minutes. An older server whose state omits custody.qa_hosts keeps the earlier rule. A consumed QA_HOST lease whose holder is parked, process-exited or ended also shows in the steering report as a Test Machine ALARM line naming the holder, its silence and when upkeep returns the host, with the steering release command; a holder with a recent subagent call or custody-checked execution heartbeat raises no Test Machine alarm. A running turn newer than the last recorded death proves presence before a tool call completes. The idle clock for a consumed lease includes tool calls by the session and its subagents, host operations on that lease, and the heartbeat of the live execution using it as a driver or companion lease; the fleet watch's idle-holder alarm covers live sessions holding a QA host whether or not they hold an item claim (items=none). When the holder also owns an active or walking QA execution silent 20 minutes, the line carries stale_walk=<id>:<N>m in place of a separate stale-walk line.
